root_idea.summary: The root centers on slowness or falling behind; ethically, sin is understood as conduct that holds a person back from good and reward.
root_idea.development: The concrete sense of sluggish movement develops into falling into sin, being burdened with sin, abstaining from sin, and the requital associated with sin.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun إِثْم is a distinct lexical headword.
أَثَام is independently attested in the Quran with the meaning of requital or punishment for sin.
أَثِيم is an independently attested adjective meaning sinful or burdened with sin.
آثِم is an active participle with the distinct citation-form meaning one who bears or incurs sin.
تَأْثِيم is an independently attested verbal noun associated with sin or sinful speech.

senses.definition: Sin, crime, fault, offense, or an act of disobedience—an unlawful act for which blame or punishment is incurred and which holds one back from reward.
senses.usage_conditions: The general Quranic moral category of sinful conduct; it may be attributed to an act, speech, or course of conduct. In discussions of wine and gambling, it denotes their sinful aspect rather than ordinarily naming those things themselves.

senses.definition: The punishment or requital resulting from sin.
senses.usage_conditions: A less usual Quran-associated interpretation recorded for the noun; the historical citation in the lexical evidence is not converted here into a modern verse location.

senses.definition: Requital, recompense, or punishment for sin.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression at 25:68, the dominant lexical interpretation is the punishment or requital resulting from sins. An alternative interpretation understands the expression as referring to a consequence leading to the commission of further sins.

senses.definition: Sinful; burdened with sin; one who commits sin, sometimes with the force of habitual or excessive sinning.
senses.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a person as characterized by sin or heavily burdened with it; the habitual or intensive nuance is supported in some classical explanations but need not apply in every occurrence.
This is a Quran-associated lexical interpretation preserved from the evidence; its historical Lane citation is not securely matched to a supplied modern QAC word location.

senses.definition: One who bears or incurs sin; a sinner.
senses.usage_conditions: An active-participial description of a person who has incurred or carries sin.

senses.definition: Sin or sinful speech, including speech that entails or ascribes sin.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of sinful discourse or the verbal ascription of sin; the Quranic contexts deny such speech in the setting described.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall into sin; to commit a sin or other unlawful act.
To reckon someone guilty of sin, punish or requite him for it, or declare him a sinner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive usage in which a person or act is judged in relation to sin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tell someone that he has sinned or to charge him with sin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II verbal usage; its verbal noun is associated with تَأْثِيم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to fall into sin.
To abstain from sin, withdraw from it, repent, and seek forgiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V reflexive usage, describing separation from or avoidance of sin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sin or sinful acts, used synonymously with إِثْم.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic nominal use distinct from the Quranic interpretation of أَثَام as punishment or requital.
A tropical, non-primary use motivated by the sinfulness of drinking wine rather than by the ordinary meaning of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stake-contending or wagering in a game of hazard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical use synonymous with gambling, motivated by the destruction of property associated with the activity.
A Classical Arabic interpretation of the noun distinct from its meaning of punishment or requital.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be slow or tardy in movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially of a she-camel's walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slow, tardy, weary, or jaded she-camel; by related adjectival usage, something slack or slow in pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete Classical Arabic usage concerning slowness of movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reckoned to have sinned, having sin reckoned against one, or requited for sin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of a person subject to a judgment or requital connected with sin.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers sinning and the synonymous sin-related nouns.
Transitive judgment, punishment, or declaration of guilt.
Slowness in the movement of a she-camel.
Core noun meaning of sin or unlawful act.
Quran-associated interpretation as punishment of sin.
Metonymic use for gambling or wagering.
Requital or punishment for sin, explicitly linked to the Quranic expression.
Classical interpretation as a valley in Hell.
Sinful or heavily sinning, with a Quran-associated liar interpretation.
Frequent or excessive commission of sin is covered by the intensive nuance of the Quranic adjective sense.
Active participle meaning one who incurs or bears sin.
Slow, weary, or tardy she-camel and related slow-paced usage.
Passive-participial description involving reckoned or requited sin.

cautions: The historical Quran citation attached to the liar interpretation of أَثِيم is not converted into a modern verse location because it does not securely match a supplied QAC occurrence.
The meanings of wine and gambling under إِثْم are explicitly marked as metonymic Classical Arabic uses, not the ordinary Quranic meaning of the noun.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane citation for the liar interpretation of أَثِيم is historically formatted and appears not to align exactly with the supplied QAC location 2:276; the interpretation is retained without assigning a modern example location.
